title: Nonderogatory to Cyclic Vector: General Case via Primary Decomposition (Axiom-Free)
description: Proves the cyclic vector theorem for ALL nonderogatory matrices over any field K, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, using primary decomposition via Bezout projections. Given minpoly(M) = ∏ p_i^{e_i} (pairwise coprime prime powers), constructs a cyclic vector v = ∑ F_i(M)w_i (F_i = complementary product). Supersedes WIP01 by eliminating the rational canonical form axiom.

overview.historicalContext: The cyclic vector theorem for nonderogatory matrices is a cornerstone of rational canonical form theory, dating to Frobenius (1879). A matrix M over a field K is nonderogatory if minpoly(M) = charpoly(M), equivalently if K^n is a cyclic K[X]-module. The classical proof uses the structure theorem for finitely generated modules over K[X] (a PID), which was unavailable in Mathlib 4.26. WIP01 (this problem's predecessor) reduced the theorem to a precisely-stated axiom: 'nonderogatory matrices are similar to their companion matrix'. WIP02 proved the squarefree case axiom-free, and WIP03 proved the prime power case axiom-free. This file (WIP04) combines these into a complete axiom-free proof for arbitrary minpoly factored into prime powers. The key innovation is that no module-structure theorem is needed: a direct construction via Bezout projections suffices.
overview.problemStatement: For a nonderogatory n×n matrix M over any field K whose minimal polynomial factors as ∏_{i < k} p_i^{e_i} (pairwise coprime, p_i irreducible monic, e_i ≥ 1), prove that M has a cyclic vector: a vector v such that no nonzero polynomial of degree < n annihilates v under M.
overview.proofStrategy:
Two-phase construction using primary decomposition via Bezout:

Phase 1 (Primary vectors): For each i, let F_i = ∏_{j≠i} p_j^{e_j}. Since deg(p_i^{e_i-1} · F_i) < n = deg(minpoly), the matrix p_i^{e_i-1}(M) · F_i(M) is nonzero, so pick w_i with this matrix not killing w_i. Set v_i = F_i(M)w_i. By construction:
- p_i^{e_i}(M)v_i = 0  (minpoly kills everything)
- p_i^{e_i-1}(M)v_i ≠ 0  (by choice)
By WIP03's key lemma: r(M)v_i = 0 implies p_i^{e_i} | r.

Phase 2 (CRT combination): Set v = ∑_i v_i. If r(M)v = 0 with deg(r) < n, use IsCoprime(p_i^{e_i}, F_i) to extract Bezout a_i · p_i^{e_i} + b_i · F_i = 1. The Bezout projection π_i = b_i(M) · F_i(M) satisfies π_i(v_i) = v_i and π_i(v_j) = 0 for j ≠ i (since p_j^{e_j} | F_i). Then r(M)v_i = π_i(r(M)v) = 0 for all i. By Phase 1: p_i^{e_i} | r for all i. By pairwise coprimality: ∏ p_i^{e_i} = minpoly | r, giving deg(r) ≥ n. Contradiction.
keyInsights: The construction v_i = F_i(M)w_i places v_i in the 'primary component' of p_i^{e_i} without needing to know the primary subspace has dimension deg(p_i^{e_i}). Only the annihilation/non-annihilation properties are used.
WIP03's key lemma (pow_irred_dvd_of_annihilated) is the engine: it replaces the PID structure theorem for the prime power case with an elementary inductive divisibility argument.
The Bezout projection trick (IsCoprime.prod_right + bezout_proj_identity) correctly isolates each primary component without needing explicit direct sum decomposition.
Polynomial commutativity (aeval_mul_comm) is used repeatedly: r(M) and F_i(M) commute because both are polynomials in M. This lets π_i 'pass through' r(M).
Finset.prod_dvd_of_coprime closes the proof cleanly: pairwise coprimality + each p_i^{e_i} | r gives ∏ p_i^{e_i} | r, which contradicts deg(r) < n.
The degree-counting argument in hpow_Fi_deg uses Polynomial.natDegree_mul to reduce a product-degree inequality to a linear inequality that omega can handle directly.
prerequisites: Linear algebra over fields (matrix evaluation of polynomials)
Minimal and characteristic polynomials of matrices
Unique factorization in polynomial rings (K[X] is a UFD)
Bezout's identity and coprimality for polynomials
Chinese Remainder Theorem for polynomial rings

sections.title: I. Definitions
sections.summary: Defines IsCyclicVector and IsNonderogatory, consistent with WIP01-WIP03.
sections.mathContext: A vector v is cyclic for M if no nonzero polynomial of degree < n annihilates v via M. A matrix is nonderogatory if its minimal polynomial equals its characteristic polynomial.

sections.title: II. Utility Lemmas
sections.summary: Seven private lemmas: irreducible_dvd_of_annihilated (Bezout coprimality), exists_mulVec_ne_zero (nonzero matrix has nontrivial image), aeval_ne_zero_of_lt_minpoly (minimality of minpoly), aeval_mul_comm (polynomial commutativity in M), bezout_proj_identity (CRT projection identity), pow_irred_dvd_of_annihilated (prime power divisibility by induction, from WIP03), mulVec_finset_sum (mulVec distributes over finite sums).
sections.mathContext: These are the same or analogous lemmas from WIP02/WIP03, gathered into a single self-contained file. pow_irred_dvd_of_annihilated is the core engine: it embeds the inductive argument from WIP03 that replaces the PID structure theorem.

sections.title: III. Main Theorem — General Nonderogatory Case
sections.summary: Proves nonderogatory_general_has_cyclic_vector: for nonderogatory M with minpoly = ∏ p_i^{e_i} (k pairwise coprime prime powers, each e_i ≥ 1), M has a cyclic vector over any field K.
sections.mathContext: The proof constructs primary vectors v_i = F_i(M)w_i, then combines them as v = ∑ v_i. The CRT projection argument extracts r(M)v_i = 0 from r(M)v = 0, the pow_irred_dvd lemma gives p_i^{e_i} | r, and pairwise coprimality gives minpoly | r, contradicting deg(r) < n.

sections.title: IV. Commentary
sections.summary: Discussion of completeness (UFD factorization would give fully general theorem), technical insight (avoiding PID module theory), and how WIP04 supersedes WIP01.
sections.mathContext: WIP04 combined with K[X] UFD factorization (available in Mathlib) would give a fully general axiom-free proof. The remaining step (factoring minpoly K M automatically) uses UniqueFactorizationMonoid but does not require the PID structure theorem for modules.

conclusion.summary: WIP04 provides a complete axiom-free Lean proof of the nonderogatory cyclic vector theorem for matrices with factored minpoly. It combines the squarefree techniques from WIP02 (Bezout projections, CRT) with the prime power engine from WIP03 (inductive divisibility) into a single clean primary decomposition argument. The result supersedes WIP01 by eliminating the rational canonical form axiom.
conclusion.implications: The primary decomposition approach demonstrated here — constructing cyclic vectors for each prime power factor via complementary products, then combining via Bezout projections — is a general strategy that avoids needing the full PID module structure theorem. This approach could generalize to other structured linear algebra settings where primary decomposition is available but the full classification theorem is not.
openQuestions: Can the factorization hypotheses (p : Fin k → K[X], e : Fin k → ℕ, ...) be eliminated by automatically factoring minpoly K M using the UFD structure of K[X]? This would give a fully general theorem from just IsNonderogatory M.
Does this primary decomposition approach generalize to modules over other PIDs (e.g., ℤ[X]-modules), or are field-specific properties essential?

crossReferences.description: Parent: the general nonderogatory cyclic vector theorem with sorry. WIP04 proves the theorem axiom-free for factored minpoly.
WIP01: full theorem with 1 axiom (rational canonical form). WIP04 eliminates this axiom via direct primary decomposition.
WIP03: prime power case (axiom-free). WIP04 generalizes WIP03 to arbitrary minpoly via CRT combination of primary vectors.
WIP02: squarefree case (axiom-free). WIP04 generalizes the Bezout/CRT technique from WIP02 to the prime power setting.

The Cayley-Hamilton theorem (charpoly(M) annihilates M) is the foundation: minpoly | charpoly, so nonderogatory means minpoly = charpoly, and the cyclic vector theorem characterizes when K^n is cyclic over K[X].

references.note: Introduced the rational canonical form and the notion of nonderogatory matrices. The cyclic vector theorem proved here is equivalent to Frobenius's characterization of nonderogatory matrices as those similar to a single companion matrix block.

references.title: Linear Algebra
references.note: Chapter 7 develops the primary decomposition theorem and rational canonical form for linear operators. The classical proof uses the structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID — the approach this formalization avoids via direct Bezout projection construction.
